Museum Quiet Bags 004

Our class visits a room of old musical instruments. The guide gives each pair of children a paper bag. Inside are two safe things to touch: a piece of wood and a piece of metal. The real instruments stay behind glass. We shake neither the bags nor the instruments. We touch the two small pieces and guess which feels colder. Then we write one word about each piece. At the end, we return the pieces to the guide but keep the paper bags for our notes.

Camera Club No Faces 004

The camera club wants to show a school day through photographs without showing anyone’s face. Mina photographs shoes waiting outside the dance room. Leo photographs open lunch boxes, but he asks their owners first. Hana takes a picture of shadows in the playground. At first, the club plans to put the photographer’s full name below each picture. Some pupils prefer not to share their names publicly, so the club uses short chosen names. The teacher keeps a private list so pupils can still collect their own prints. The exhibition will be in the entrance hall for one week. Visitors may look at the pictures, but they must ask before copying them.

originalGroup.material:
Bus Shelter Library 004

A small book box stands beside the village bus shelter. People may take a book and bring it back when they finish. They do not have to leave another book immediately. A notebook inside records titles, not borrowers’ names. The volunteer says this makes the box easy to use, but it also means she cannot contact someone about an overdue book.
After a week of heavy rain, two books become damp. The volunteer moves the box under the shelter roof and puts a "Please close the door" note on it. The village school offers to donate a shelf. She thanks the school but asks for a smaller shelf because the first one would block the path to the bus. The box reopens on Monday with dry books and a clear path.

originalGroup.material:
Garden Weather Log 004

The gardening club compared two tomato beds. Both received the same number of seeds from the same packet. Bed A was near a wall, while Bed B was in an open corner. Members planned to compare how many seeds grew. During the first week, a pipe leaked beside Bed A. That bed received more water even though the pupils used the same watering cans.
When more seeds grew in Bed A, one pupil said the wall must be the reason. The club leader disagreed. They had not kept water conditions the same, so the result could not show the effect of the wall alone. The group still recorded the numbers and the leak. They repaired the pipe and planned another trial. Their report included the first trial because an unexpected problem could help the next group plan more carefully.

They had not kept water conditions the same, so the result could not show the effect of the wall alone. The group still recorded the numbers and the leak. They repaired the pipe and planned another trial. Their report included the first trial because an unexpected problem could help the next group plan more carefully.

originalGroup.material:
Sound Map Walk 004

For a neighbourhood project, pupils made a map of sounds along a walking route. They marked a fountain, a bicycle crossing and a shop door that rang when it opened. They recorded short clips on a school device. The teacher asked them to avoid recording private conversations.
At the crossing, traffic was so loud that the bicycle signal was hard to hear. Rather than move the microphone closer to a passing rider, the pupils wrote a note describing the problem. Later they asked the road office for the signal’s official timing. They added this information in a different colour so readers could tell it had not come from their own recording.
One street on the final map had no clips. It passed a health centre where people might talk about private matters. The pupils marked it "No recording here" and explained the reason. A visitor said the map looked incomplete. The teacher replied that leaving out a recording could be a thoughtful choice. The class had to show where their evidence came from and respect people along the route.
